experiments.question: Does an adaptive retrieval loop repair seeded context failures better than the fixed initial recipe on the sanitized benchmark?
experiments.hypothesis: Changing retrieval behavior after diagnosis improves evidence-grounded task score on seeded failures.
experiments.independent_variable: fixed initial retrieval recipe vs adaptive repair recipe
experiments.baseline: first pass on 12 sanitized fixture cases
experiments.treatment: critic diagnosis plus Loop Doctor retrieval-policy mutation and rerun
experiments.stop_rule: done when all seeded cases have deterministic pass-to-pass evidence and no unsupported success claim

experiments.question: How sensitive is answer quality to the reasoning provider when every provider receives the same evidence packet?
experiments.hypothesis: Provider/model choice changes synthesis quality less than context quality on the seeded retrieval failures.
experiments.baseline: one fixed provider/model over frozen evidence packets
experiments.treatment: Gemini, OpenAI, W&B Inference, TypeSafe, or other available adapters over identical packets
experiments.dataset_or_cases: held subset of sanitized WorldLoop cases with frozen evidence snapshots
experiments.stop_rule: stop after each selected provider has one reproducible run per case; do not tune prompts per-provider during the comparison

experiments.question: Can a typed fixed-evidence reader fix failures that are actually interpretation/schema failures without adding retrieval depth?
experiments.hypothesis: Some apparent retrieval failures disappear when the same evidence is read through typed obligations instead of naive concatenation.
experiments.treatment: typed evidence-obligation reader over exactly the same evidence
experiments.dataset_or_cases: fixed-evidence cases including a multi-facet/ambiguous case
experiments.stop_rule: do not add graph/traversal until same-evidence reader ablation is adjudicated

experiments.question: Which retrieval operators actually contribute to correction on each failure class?
experiments.hypothesis: Temporal and graph operators help only their corresponding demonstrated failure classes; adding every operator increases cost without universal gains.
experiments.treatment: exact, lexical, vector, temporal, graph and selected combinations
experiments.stop_rule: retain an operator only when it improves a predeclared metric on its target class without unacceptable regression

experiments.question: Can Weave make the failure-to-repair trajectory inspectable and comparable across loop versions?
experiments.hypothesis: Trajectory-level logging makes Compiler planning, pass-1 failure, Critic diagnosis, Loop Doctor mutation, pass-2 improvement, latency and scores reviewable in one evaluation surface.
experiments.treatment: Weave traced agent-role spans plus evaluation rows/summary
experiments.dataset_or_cases: seeded failure cases, starting with case-cross-entity
experiments.stop_rule: one complete inspectable three-role trajectory plus aggregate comparison is enough for hackathon MVP

experiments.question: Can Gemini on Mac and an OCI provider independently continue from the same LifeOps durable state without chat-history dependence?
experiments.hypothesis: Both providers can resolve the same project/checkpoint and emit compatible typed run records through the shared LifeOps loop.
experiments.treatment: Gemini CLI on Mac and governed OCI worker starting from the same resolved LifeOps object refs
experiments.dataset_or_cases: WorldLoop project/checkpoint canary; no private corpus required
experiments.stop_rule: pass when both providers independently resolve the same refs and a typed non-authoritative delta round-trips

experiments.question: Does the same loop generalize from sanitized fixtures to source-backed changing-world evidence?
experiments.hypothesis: A source-authority-preserving LifeOps/BTW adapter can reuse the same evaluation contract without making private data a hidden demo dependency.
experiments.treatment: optional hackathon-built read-only adapter to pre-existing LifeOps/BTW
experiments.dataset_or_cases: small reviewed public-safe/live seed plus fixture fallback
experiments.stop_rule: skip for judging if source permissions, provenance, or human review are not ready; never expose private data

experiments.question: Do prior WorldLoop failure trajectories produce a policy/program that improves first-pass behavior on unseen tasks?
experiments.hypothesis: A candidate context/resource/workflow policy derived only from training trajectories reduces held-out routing/context regret or improves first-pass verified success without reducing final correctness.
experiments.baseline: v0 on a frozen held-out task/entity/time split
experiments.treatment: v1 derived from training-split failure classes/counterfactual outcomes
experiments.dataset_or_cases: new train/held-out split derived from sanitized/synthetic WorldLoop cases; held-out cluster identities must not appear in policy training
experiments.stop_rule: promote only if a predeclared primary metric improves without a verified-correctness or fail-closed regression; otherwise reject/rollback

experiments.question: Can WorldLoop causally distinguish when task-relevant knowledge is available in model parameters (W), active context (C), or external memory (M), and learn to allocate those resources?
experiments.hypothesis: On a synthetic world absent from pretraining, independent W/C/M interventions produce distinguishable behavioral regimes and a resource policy can reduce unnecessary context/retrieval while preserving verified correctness.
experiments.baseline: base open model with W=0, C=0, M=0 and controlled individual arms
experiments.treatment: LoRA on/off for W, explicit prompt context for C, controlled external memory for M, plus conflicts such as stale W/current M
experiments.dataset_or_cases: synthetic fictional world with train/held-out entity and fact splits
experiments.stop_rule: do not claim physical weight knowledge for hosted models; LoRA intervention must be reproducible and held-out facts/tasks must remain uncontaminated
experiments.artifact: marimo W/C/M cube + Weave evaluation + optional W&B model artifact

experiments.question: Can ARIA use real WorldLoop Weave results to propose a bounded experiment that improves the incumbent policy/program?
experiments.hypothesis: ARIA can identify a non-obvious failure cluster or performance driver and propose a testable graph/node/policy/data/config change that can be evaluated against the frozen incumbent.
experiments.treatment: one ARIA-derived hypothesis implemented as a bounded candidate
experiments.dataset_or_cases: WorldLoop Weave trajectories and held-out evaluation
experiments.stop_rule: one real hypothesis-to-experiment-to-evaluation cycle is sufficient; do not use ARIA only as a report summarizer

experiments.question: Can WorldLoop progressively compile successful open-ended agent behavior into a smaller typed workflow while preserving held-out verified success?
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing broad/open-loop reasoning with deterministic transitions or narrow typed semantic primitives reduces semantic-surface ratio and execution variance without degrading verified correctness.
experiments.independent_variable: open exploratory execution vs compiled typed workflow version
experiments.baseline: a traced workflow requiring broad model-owned routing/reasoning
experiments.treatment: a candidate typed graph that replaces at least one broad semantic/open-loop step with deterministic logic or a bounded semantic primitive and explicit transition
experiments.dataset_or_cases: a small repeated-task family with frozen held-out variants so graph compilation cannot overfit one exact trajectory
experiments.stop_rule: accept the compiled candidate only if semantic surface or execution variance decreases while verified correctness and guardrails remain non-inferior on held-out variants
experiments.artifact: reports/experiments/EXP-011.json + marimo before/after graph + Weave traces
